title: Poverty
note: Poverty is having none of the things that can be enjoyed.

couplets.plain: What hurts like poverty? Only poverty hurts like poverty.
couplets.pm: If you ask what hurts a person as much as poverty does, the answer is poverty and nothing else. Nothing even equals it, so there is no need to say that nothing is worse.

couplets.plain: The sinner called poverty comes and leaves you with neither the next world nor this one.
couplets.pm: When the sinner called poverty comes to someone, it leaves him with no joy in the next world and none in this one. He can’t give, so he loses the next, and he can’t enjoy, so he loses this.

couplets.plain: The craving called poverty destroys, all at once, your old family standing and your fine speech.
couplets.pm: The craving called poverty destroys at once the old standing of the family it seizes and the speech that goes with it. Without craving there is no poverty, so poverty is called craving. It brings low work and shameful words its forebears never knew. He rejects taking “skin” as the body, since saying it ruins the body has no point.
couplets.note: தோல் is literally skin. He reads it as refined speech, and the plain reading follows him.
couplets.sensitive: says poverty strips the poor of dignity

links.quote: destroys, all at once, your old family standing and your fine speech
links.reason: Poverty can destroy even the standing and speech a family has handed down.

couplets.plain: Even in those of good family, poverty brings a weakness from which shameful words are born.
couplets.pm: Even in those of good family, from whom shameful words never come, poverty brings the weakness that gives rise to them. The shameful words are “Give to us.” The weakness is forgetting your birth now and then in the depth of your pain, and thinking of saying them.
couplets.sensitive: says want reduces people to grovelling

links.quote: Even in those of good family, poverty brings a weakness

couplets.plain: In the one misery called poverty, many miseries come and settle.
couplets.pm: Within the single misery called poverty, many miseries quickly arise. From it come, day after day, the pain of going to rich men’s doors, of seeing them, of being refused, of taking what they give if they don’t refuse, and of carrying it off to scrape together what you need.

links.reason: Opens the one misery called poverty and finds many miseries packed inside.

couplets.plain: Even if they know a good truth well and say it, the words of the poor lose their meaning.
couplets.pm: Even if the poor know the truth of the true books clearly and speak it, their words come to nothing. People fear that if they listen gladly, they will feel bound to meet the speaker’s needs, so no one listens and the words are wasted. Even learning is no use.
couplets.sensitive: tells the poor their words count for nothing

links.quote: the words of the poor lose their meaning

couplets.plain: A man whose poverty has no righteousness to it is looked at as a stranger, even by the mother who bore him.
couplets.pm: A man whose poverty has no tie to righteousness, as neither its cause nor its result, is regarded as a stranger even by his mother, whose loving-kindness is natural. There is nothing to get from him and something he will need, so all his kin abandon him.
couplets.sensitive: calls the poor wretches even a mother would disown

links.quote: even by the mother who bore him
links.reason: Poverty without righteousness can part a man from the very mother who bore him.

couplets.plain: Will it come today too, the poverty that all but killed me yesterday?
couplets.pm: Poverty made me suffer yesterday as if it had killed me. Must it come to me today as well? If it does, what will I do? This is the voice of a man who only just managed to fill his stomach yesterday.
couplets.sensitive: voices despair at poverty as daily near-death

links.quote: the poverty that all but killed me yesterday

couplets.plain: You can sleep even in the middle of a fire. In poverty there is no sleep at all.
couplets.pm: With spells and drugs, a man can lie and sleep in the middle of a fire. Once poverty comes, there is no sleep by any means. Poverty is crueller than fire. The same poor man is speaking.

links.quote: In poverty there is no sleep at all
sleep even in the middle of a fire

couplets.plain: If those who have nothing don’t give up everything, they are only the death of salt and gruel.
couplets.pm: For those with nothing to enjoy, the one thing left to do is to give up everything. If they don’t, they are death to the salt and gruel in others’ houses. Their kin have already left them, so to keep their honour they must give up the body too. Some say it means giving up in the mind what is left.
couplets.note: “Give up everything” can mean renouncing the world. He takes it as giving up the body too.
couplets.sensitive: reads as telling the destitute to give up life

links.quote: If those who have nothing don’t give up everything
links.reason: Paints having nothing as a dead end: give up everything, or be the death of salt and gruel.

ideaLinks.quote: your old family standing and your fine speech
ideaLinks.reason: Poverty destroys the old standing and fine speech that a good birth passes down.

ideaLinks.quote: a weakness from which shameful words are born
